name.text: Evaluate the Definite integral using integration by parts

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

This is a definite integral, but first, we need to compute it like any other indefinite integral. Then substitute the limits of integration later towards the end.

The first step here is to pick \(u\) and \(dv\) so that when we compute \(du\) and \(v\)

\(\displaystyle u = {@func_var_u@}, \; dv ={@func_var_dv@} dx\).

\(\displaystyle du = {@diff_u@} dx, \; v= {@int_v@}\)

We need to plug in the above and use the integration-by-parts formula as follows:

\( \displaystyle \int udv = u \cdot v - \int vdu\)

\( \begin{align} \displaystyle \int_{@lower_limit@}^{@upper_limit@}({@func_var_u@})\cdot {@func_var_dv@} dx & = \left [({@func_var_u@})\cdot({@int_v@}) \right ]_{@lower_limit@}^{@upper_limit@}-\int_{@lower_limit@}^{@upper_limit@}({@int_v@}){@diff_u@} dx \\ & = \displaystyle \left ({@func_subt_upper_limit@}-{@func_subt_lower_limit@}\right ) -\left [ {@int_v_du@} \right ]_{@lower_limit@}^{@upper_limit@} \\ & = \displaystyle \left ({@func_subt_upper_limit@}-{@func_subt_lower_limit@}\right )- \left ({@func_subt_upper_limit_1@}-{@func_subt_lower_limit_1@}\right) \\ & = \displaystyle {@ta@} \end{align}\)

Because \(\displaystyle \int_a^b e^{u}du=\left [ \frac{1}{u^{\prime}}e^{u}\right ]_a^b\)
